receive shift register will destroy the received byte and must be avoided.
be low. SS must remain low until the transmission is complete. If SS goes high, the SPI is forced into idle

must_have_properties: Identical CPOL on master and communicating slave
Master must always drive SCK; slave must never drive SCK
Slave SS must remain LOW for the entire 8-bit transfer (CPHA=0 strict; CPHA=1 may stay LOW back-to-back)
In master mode, any change to {CPOL, CPHA, SSOE, LSBFE, MODFEN, SPC0, BIDIROE, SPPR, SPR} mid-transmission MUST abort the transmission and force the SPI into idle state
In slave mode, any change to {CPOL, CPHA, SSOE, LSBFE, MODFEN, SPC0, BIDIROE} mid-transmission corrupts the transmission and MUST be avoided
CPOL or MSTR bit change with a received byte pending in the receive shift register destroys the received byte and MUST be avoided
SPIF clearing requires read of SPISR (with SPIF=1) followed by read of SPIDR
SPTEF clearing requires read of SPISR (with SPTEF=1) followed by write to SPIDR; a SPIDR write without first reading SPTEF=1 is silently ignored
MODF clearing requires read of SPISR (with MODF=1) followed by write to SPICR1
must_not_have_properties: Two simultaneous masters driving MOSI/SCK without mode-fault arbitration
Two slaves both selected on the same MISO line (output contention)

compliance_failure_modes.trigger: Third byte received while SPIF still set and not serviced before start of third transmission.
SS pulled LOW while configured master + MODFEN=1.

fields.min_baud_rate_constraint: Implementation-defined per SoC; spec note: max allowed baud rate per SoC SPI Electrical Specification.
fields.reset_behavior_compliance: After reset SPE=0, SPTEF=1, SPIF=0, MODF=0, MSTR=0, CPOL=1, CPHA=0, all data registers cleared.
